metric: mean item score in [0,1]: exact/numeric 0 or 1, extraction share of fields, rubric judge score / 2

run_notes.note: run-3 responses (max_output_tokens 2048) with empty replies retried at a larger budget; see repaired_with_max_output_tokens on each row.

params.rubric_scale:
2 = the reply meets every criterion.
1 = the reply meets some criteria but misses at least one, and has no serious violation.
0 = the reply meets fewer than half the criteria, OR seriously violates a "never / does not / without" criterion (for example asks for an OTP, PIN or password, or invents a specific date or promise).

verification.statement: The "verified": true flags were set by an AI assistant (Claude) at the dataset owner's request, not by a human reviewer. Each task was confirmed in one of two ways; anything that could not be confirmed was left false.

rows.method: Recomputed with separate exact-fraction code (not the generator). Income-tax slabs, the 87A rebate (nil tax up to 12,00,000) and the 75,000 standard deduction match PIB / Income Tax Department pages; tax at 16,00,000 reproduces the published 1,20,000.

Invoices and bank statements were re-parsed from the prompt text and recomputed line by line (line amounts, discounts, GST, grand totals, running balances). Rent-agreement values were checked against the clauses in the prompt.
Read and judged independently (intent / sentiment / language labels; 9 days > 7-day window).
Every extracted value was checked to occur verbatim in the customer message.
Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.69 (two years) and s.41 (45 days; 50% pre-deposit) match the statute text as quoted on legal-database mirrors; the India Code pages were unreachable.
Thresholds (District <= 50 lakh, State 50 lakh–2 crore, National > 2 crore, by consideration paid) read in the Rules, 2021 text (copy hosted on thc.nic.in).
RTI Rules 2012 PDF on cic.gov.in (application fee ₹10; BPL exempt).
Code on Social Security 2020 text read directly (s.53, s.60).

RBI TAT table (Circular of 20 Sep 2019), RBI limited-liability circular (6 Jul 2017) and RBI KYC FAQs read directly; compensation arithmetic recomputed. "Plain days" for T+N follows the circular's "T = calendar date".
RBI Integrated Ombudsman FAQ (30-day no-reply ground).

verification.held_back: hin-016 – hin-020 and pay-020: the six rubric tasks. Their criteria are judgement calls and the LLM judge has not been validated against human grades. A human spot-check is still pending: a flag only means the assistant could confirm the answer, not that a person signed off.

law_policy.prompt: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, within how many years from the date the cause of action arose must a consumer complaint ordinarily be filed? Reply with only the number.
law_policy.worked_solution: Section 69: a Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose.

law_policy.prompt: A consumer received a defective washing machine and the cause of action arose on 10 January 2024. They file a complaint on 5 March 2026. Assuming no application to condone delay is made, is the complaint within the limitation period of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019? Reply with only yes or no.
law_policy.worked_solution: Limitation is two years (section 69): it ended on 10 January 2026. 5 March 2026 is after that date, so the complaint is late: no.

law_policy.prompt: A consumer paid exactly ₹50,00,000 (₹50 lakh) as consideration for a service and wants to file a complaint. Under the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, which Consumer Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction? Reply with only one of: District, State, National.
law_policy.worked_solution: The District Commission's limit is 'does not exceed' ₹50 lakh, so exactly ₹50 lakh is still within the District Commission; the State Commission starts above ₹50 lakh.

payments_banking.prompt: A customer sends ₹5,000 by UPI to a friend. The money is debited from their account but the friend's account is not credited. The bank reverses the money on T+4. T is the day of the transaction; count plain days and ignore holidays. Using the RBI TAT framework (auto-reversal by T+1, ₹100 per day of delay beyond that), how much compensation in rupees is the customer owed? Reply with only the number.
payments_banking.worked_solution: UPI fund transfer, debited but not credited: auto-reversal due by T+1; compensation ₹100 per day beyond T+1. Reversal on T+4 is 3 days late → 3 × ₹100 = ₹300.

payments_banking.prompt: A customer pays a merchant by UPI. The account is debited but no confirmation reaches the merchant, and the bank auto-reverses the money on T+5. T is the day of the transaction; count plain days and ignore holidays. Under the RBI TAT framework (UPI merchant payments: auto-reversal within T+5, ₹100 per day of delay beyond that), how much compensation in rupees is owed? Reply with only the number.
payments_banking.worked_solution: UPI merchant payment: auto-reversal within T+5. Reversal on T+5 is on time, so there is no delay and compensation is ₹0.

payments_banking.prompt: Per the RBI framework on turnaround time (TAT) for failed transactions, by which day (counted from the transaction day T) must a bank complete the auto-reversal when a UPI fund transfer debits the sender but does not credit the beneficiary? Reply in the form T+N, e.g. T+2.
payments_banking.worked_solution: UPI transfer of funds, account debited but beneficiary not credited: auto-reversal by the beneficiary bank latest on T+1.
